title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When you one-hot encode, each unique item in your data gets its own dimension. For example, if you have $$4$$ unique items, you'll have $$4$$ dimensions. Think about how many unique 6-letter combinations can be formed from the letters T, G, C, and A.

title: Calculating Combinations
text: Consider how many different ways you can arrange $$6$$ letters where each letter can be T, G, C, or A. This will give you the number of unique 6-letter combinations.

title: Calculate the Number of 6-Letter Combinations
text: How many unique 6-letter combinations can be formed using the letters T, G, C, and A?

title: Connecting Combinations to Dimensions
text: Each unique 6-letter combination corresponds to a dimension in your one-hot encoding. If you know the number of unique combinations, you know the number of dimensions.

title: Determine the Total Dimensions
text: If each DNA string is $$3000$$ letters long, how many 6-letter combinations can you extract from it?
